meta.source: Reserve Bank of India, DBIE (via the Data Bank)
meta.revisionPolicy: Each year passes through three stages: the budget estimate (February before the year), the revised estimate (February of the year) and the accounts (provisional in May after the year, audited later). The RBI's tables restate a year as it moves from one stage to the next; each stage is kept as its own series.
meta.coverage: The Centre's short-term borrowing: 91, 182 and 364-day Treasury bills and cash management bills outstanding, and who holds them, every Friday since May 2006
meta.note: RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement table 13, Government of India Treasury Bills Outstanding (DBIE report 2, provider DP1), with the Bulletin's print of the same table (report 29), which adds 14-day intermediate bills (bought only by state governments, to park surplus cash) and the weeks of January to May 2006; the two agree on all 12125 holdings both print. The RBI's own holding is listed in the table but never printed. Face value, close of business on Friday. Banks, primary dealers and state governments are holdings in SGL and CSGL accounts with the RBI (the table's note 2). Totals add the holders the table prints for that week (computed); an empty cell is not printed and is not counted. A holding printed below zero cannot be true and is left empty, with no total that week: 14-day intermediate Treasury bills, Others, 2026-09-25: -182118.66; 14-day intermediate Treasury bills, Others, 2026-09-25: -182118.66; 14-day intermediate Treasury bills, Others, 2026-09-18: -179638.79; 14-day intermediate Treasury bills, Others, 2026-09-18: -179638.79.
